{
  "decision": "APPLY",
  "workflow_yaml": "name: website
on: workflow_dispatch
jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20.x
      - name: Generate API docs
        working-directory: website/generate-api-docs
        run: make all
      - name: Build website
        working-directory: website
        run: |
          npm ci
          npm run build
      - name: Deploy to GitHub Pages
        uses: peaceiris/actions-gh-pages@v3
        with:
          github_token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          publish_dir: ./website/docs/.vitepress/dist
          cname: fxts.dev
          user_name: github-actions[bot]
          user_email: 41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com",
  "rationale": "The workflow has a single build job with representative successful-duration history (four successful workflow_dispatch runs around 80 seconds each), satisfying the P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT precondition that representative successful-duration history exists. Adding timeout-minutes bounds runaway job consumption without removing or altering any checkout, setup, docs generation, build, or deploy step, so intended build/test/deploy coverage is preserved. A 10-minute budget provides roughly 7x headroom over observed successful runs, accommodating cold dependency installation while preventing a hung job from consuming unlimited runner time. No permissions are weakened, no secrets or new network access are added, and the deployment step is unchanged.",
  "evidence_ids": ["pattern:P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT", "experiment:batch-interactive-three--fb8b16eb65a11508"]
}
